title: Solving x² = p and x³ = p
keyIdea: x² = p has two solutions, ±√p, when p is positive; x³ = p has exactly one, ∛p.

kid: 6 × 6 = 36. But −6 × −6 = 36 too! So x² = 36 has two answers: 6 and −6.
For cubes, 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, but −3 cubed is −27. So x³ = 27 has just one answer, 3.
To undo a square, use a square root and remember the ± sign. To undo a cube, use a cube root.
adult: To solve x² = p, take the square root of both sides and keep both signs: x = ±√p. If p is negative there is no real answer, because a square is never negative.
To solve x³ = p, take the cube root: x = ∛p. Cubes keep the sign, so ∛(−8) = −2. Some roots, like √2, are irrational. Their decimals never end or repeat.

familyTip: Draw y = x² and a flat line y = 9 on squared paper. Where do they meet?

practice.prompt: x² = {=r*r}. What is the positive solution?
practice.hint: Ask: which positive number times itself makes {=r*r}? That is the square root.
practice.explain: The square root of {=r*r} is {r}, so x = {r} or x = −{r}. The positive one is {r}.

practice.hint: Ask: which number times itself three times makes {=r*r*r}? That is the cube root.
practice.explain: The cube root of {=r*r*r} is {r}, because {r} × {r} × {r} = {=r*r*r}. A cube has only one real root.

practice.prompt: How many real solutions does x² = 49 have?
practice.hint: 7 × 7 = 49. Can a negative number squared also make 49?
practice.explain: Both 7 × 7 and −7 × −7 make 49, so there are two solutions: 7 and −7.
A square is never negative, so there is no real solution.

pool.prompt: x² = {=r*r}. What is the negative solution?
pool.hint: Find the square root, then put a minus sign in front of it.
pool.explain: The square root of {=r*r} is {r}, so the negative solution is x = −{r}.

pool.prompt: x² = {=r*r}. What is the sum of the two solutions?
pool.hint: The two solutions are the same number, one positive and one negative.
pool.explain: The solutions are {r} and −{r}. Opposites always add to zero: {r} + (−{r}) = 0.

pool.prompt: On a graph of y = x², the line y = 9 crosses at…
pool.hint: The y = x² curve is a mirror image on each side of the y-axis. Which numbers squared make 9?
pool.explain: 3 × 3 = 9 and −3 × −3 = 9, so the line crosses the curve at x = −3 and x = 3.

pool.prompt: A square has area {=r*r} cm². How long is its side, in cm?

visual.caption: Drag the level line up and down. Watch where it meets y = x²: two points, one, or none.
